From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@starlake.ai>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@starlake.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 13:12:00 -0800
Subject: High 5xx + timeouts across calls to /v1/generate since ~13:30 PST

Jordan — we started seeing a spike in 5xx and timeouts around 13:30 PST today across our production turfs. Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to 12%, and throughput dropped by ~40%. We confirmed the same behavior from multiple hosts in our VPC that are peered with Redwood.

Attached: starlake-error-samples.txt, packet-capture-1103.pcap.

What we’ve tried: flushed our NAT tables, validated security groups, and nothing changed. Traces show long TCP handshakes and repeated DNS lookups for the Redwood endpoint that sometimes resolve to an IP that times out. Can you confirm if anything changed on your egress paths or if there are known issues in us-west-2? This is impacting two large jobs in flight.

Tom Reynolds
Head of Platform Ops | Starlake Analytics

Subject: Re: High 5xx + timeouts — initial network triage

Folks — quick summary of what I’m seeing from the packet capture and our server logs:
- Multiple SYN retransmits followed by long gaps; TCP sessions sometimes never complete the handshake.
- DNS: client-side lookups for api.redwood.example resolved intermittently to an IP in the customer-region edge pool that subsequently dropped traffic (ICMP unreachable / no TCP ACK).
- On our side, backends are healthy and not overloaded; retries correlate with the failed egress IPs.

Hypothesis: an egress misroute / peering flapping in the path between the Starlake peered subnet and our edge (possible transit provider or customer-side proxy). There are signs of a middlebox rewriting or proxying DNS responses intermittently.

Immediate asks:
1) Jordan — please request that Starlake validate their edge proxy/NAT logs for the timestamps 2028-11-03T13:20–13:50 PST.
2) Monica — can we provision temporary routing to alternate egress via another peering in us-west-2? That would confirm whether the issue is path-specific.

I’ll keep digging; attaching a short pcap snippet with annotated timestamps.

—Sean
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Attachments referenced: packet-capture-1103.pcap (annotated)

Tom — quick update for your ops team:
- We’ve confirmed the failure pattern correlates to a subset of egress IPs returned by DNS. Those IPs are timing out / dropping connections.
- We’re asking your network team to check for transparent proxies or firewall rules that could be rewriting DNS answers or blackholing specific upstreams.
- As a temporary mitigation, we can route Starlake traffic through an alternate peering point in us-west-2 (this will be slightly higher latency for some requests). Would you like us to flip that and validate?

If you authorize, Monica will coordinate a short cutover and validation window. Appreciate any firewall logs you can share (sample lines are fine).

Jordan

From: Akamai-NOC <noc@akamai.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@starlake.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Nov 2028 02:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [Akamai] Observed BGP flap affecting transit -> potential blackholing (log ref 78921)

Tom/Jordan — per our upstream monitoring, we observed a BGP flap on one of the transit peers serving the Starlake edge (log ref 78921) between 13:25–13:42 PST that caused intermittent announcements to withdraw. Some prefixes were momentarily unreachable from one transit, leading to asymmetric routing and packet drops.

Recommended immediate actions:
- Implement temporary prefer-route to alternate transit (we can push a change from our side if you authorize).
- Validate that any transparent proxies are not responding with stale DNS answers during the flap window.
- Collect firewall/NAT logs for 13:20–13:50 PST.

We can coordinate a quick mitigation call if helpful; please advise time.

—Akamai NOC

Attachments referenced: timeline-compact.csv (BGP events)

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: leadership@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Nov 2028 04:25:00 -0800
Subject: Exec brief: Starlake production impact — likely transit peering disruption

Team — quick executive summary:
- Impact: Starlake Analytics saw ~12% error rate and ~40% throughput degradation for ~17 minutes on 2028-11-03 starting at ~13:25 PST. Affected tenant: Starlake prod across three clusters (us-west-2).
- Root cause (current best understanding): transient BGP flap at a transit provider caused partial withdrawal of prefixes leading to blackholing and asymmetric paths; intermittent stale DNS/proxy responses on the customer side amplified failures.
- Mitigation taken: Our SREs validated healthy backends and prepared an alternate peering cutover; Akamai confirmed the BGP event and worked a prefer-route. Starlake traffic has been re-routed and error rates have normalized.
- Customer impact: brief intermittent 5xxs, jobs retried successfully for most customers; Starlake reported lost throughput on two large pipelines (internal estimate: ~3–4 hours of slowed processing across the affected jobs).
- Near-term next steps:
  1) Formal postmortem with Starlake and Akamai (owner: Monica).
  2) Offer a one-time credit and SLA exception for the event (recommended).
  3) Evaluate DNS TTL hardening and alternate peering defaults for high-sensitivity tenants.

I recommend we proactively offer Starlake a credit and schedule a joint postmortem this week. If approved, Jordan and Monica will lead the customer touch and credit logistics.

—Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Operations | Redwood Inference

- Root cause: a transient BGP flap at a transit provider combined with a customer-side proxy that responded with cached/stale DNS answers.
